questions.q: 2-Bromopentane is heated with sodium ethoxide in ethanol. The major product is:
questions.explain: A small strong base removes H from C-3 to give the more substituted (Saytzeff) alkene, mostly as the E isomer; pent-1-ene is minor.
The bulky tert-butoxide removes the more exposed CH₃ hydrogens, so the less substituted Hofmann alkene becomes major; small bases such as EtO⁻ give 2-methylbut-2-ene.

questions.q: Chloroethane is heated with alcoholic KOH. The main product and the reason are:
options: Ethene, because ethoxide in alcohol is a stronger base and elimination wins
Ethanol, because OH⁻ is a good nucleophile
Ethene, because chloroethane forms a stable carbocation
Diethyl ether, because ethoxide attacks by SN1
questions.explain: Alcoholic KOH contains ethoxide, a strong base, so E2 dehydrohalogenation gives ethene. With aqueous KOH the solvated OH⁻ acts mainly as a nucleophile and ethanol forms.

questions.q: meso-1,2-Dibromo-1,2-diphenylethane undergoes E2 with KOEt. The alkene formed is:
options: A 1 : 1 mixture of E and Z isomers
questions.explain: Because H and Br must be anti-periplanar, the meso isomer can give only the E alkene, while the (1R,2R) or (1S,2S) isomer gives only the Z alkene.
